title: kv-cache: fragmentation-aware eviction, spillover paging improvements, and background compaction scheduler
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We observed higher-than-expected memory fragmentation and tail-latency regressions on large multi-tenant hosts when the KV cache spilled to host memory and the scheduler could not compact entries during low-load windows. This PR implements three coordinated changes to improve memory efficiency and stability: 1) a fragmentation-aware eviction policy (F-A LRU) that biases eviction toward small, scattered fragments and reclaims contiguous regions preferentially; 2) a spillover paging format with aligned slab pages and a lightweight compact-on-read path to reduce page churn and IO amplification; and 3) a background compaction scheduler that opportunistically runs during predicted idle windows (using the existing batching/telemetry signals) to coalesce free fragments, reducing the need for costly runtime defragmentation. Motivation: reduce spillover-induced latency spikes and lower working set memory by 10-30% depending on workload mixture. This is part of ENG-3210 (KV cache memory management) and ENG-3285 (scheduling for background maintenance). Changes: - Implemented fragmentation scoring for cache entries and integrated into eviction decision point. The score is computed from entry size, adjacency to free pages, and age. - Reworked spillover on-disk/in-memory page format to use 64KB-aligned slab pages and added a compact-on-read fast-path for hot entries that cross page boundaries. - Added a background compaction scheduler that hooks into the continuous batching telemetry (batch occupancy and request inter-arrival times) to decide safe compaction windows. - Exposed two runtime knobs: KV_FRAGMENTATION_THRESHOLD (percent) and COMPACTION_MAX_MS_PER_WINDOW to allow controlled rollout on Dedicated/Private. - Extended metrics: kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.compaction_runs, kv_cache.spillover_io_bytes, kv_cache.eviction_fragment_hit. - Added unit and integration tests; extended perf harness with mixed-chat/long-context synthetic workload. Benchmarks: On rtx-8000 CI cluster:  - Peak tail P99 token latency reduced from 154ms -> 118ms for long-context chat workload with spillover.  - Average memory working set reduced ~18% on mixed workloads.  - Compaction CPU overhead observed ~1.2% when enabled with conservative windows. Rollout plan: Gradual rollout behind feature flag. Start with canary on low-density Dedicated hosts, monitor kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio and spillover_io_bytes, then expand. See release_notes for ops guidance.

refactor(spillover): align slab paging and add compact-on-read path
feat(scheduler): background compaction scheduler tied to batching telemetry
test(kv): unit tests for fragmentation and compaction; integration test for spillover path
docs(ops): runtime knobs and rollout notes
review_comments: David Nguyen: Overall approach looks solid. Two asks: 1) add a micro-benchmark proving compact-on-read latency for hot entries, 2) ensure the fragmentation score can't be gamed by synthetic workloads. (requested changes)
Asha Patel (author): Added micro-benchmark in perf/benchmarks and hardened score via max contribution per-sample; updated tests to include synthetic adversarial case. (reply)

Marta Lopez: Please ensure COMPACTION_MAX_MS_PER_WINDOW defaults to a conservative value and document failure modes; also prefer exponential backoff for compaction when I/O contention detected. (requested changes)
Asha Patel: Default set to 20ms per window and added backoff based on spillover_io_bytes; documented in docs/ops/kv_compaction_rollout.md. (reply)
Ethan Clark: CI flakes reproduced initially on macOS build matrix due to a timing test; switched to mocked clock for stability. Approved after fixes. (approved)
CI Bot: build/linux (passed), test/linux (passed), lint (passed), perf/regression (passed), build/macos (passed after rerun)
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: fragmentation-aware eviction, spillover page alignment, compact-on-read fast-path, and background compaction scheduler. Reduces tail latency and working set for spillover-heavy workloads. Feature gated; default conservative settings applied. See docs/ops/kv_compaction_rollout.md for rollout and monitoring guidance.
notes_for_ops: Enable behind feature flag 'kv_compaction_v1' for initial canary. Monitor metrics: kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio, kv_cache.compaction_runs, kv_cache.spillover_io_bytes, host_cpu_util. If compaction causes unexpected IO, reduce COMPACTION_MAX_MS_PER_WINDOW or increase KV_FRAGMENTATION_THRESHOLD.
